sections.h2: Which Jasper County, MO offices handle my property tax?
sections.html:
The Assessor sets the value and the Collector sends the bill and takes the money. Jasper County has Lisa Perry as Assessor and Steven E. McIntosh as Collector. Both have a presence at the Carthage courthouse, 302 S. Main, and the Collector also staffs the Joplin Courts Building at 633 S. Pearl.

  • Collector, Carthage: 417-358-0409 for personal property and 417-358-0411 for real property, Room 107
  • Collector, Joplin: 417-625-4324 for both kinds
  • Assessor, real estate: 417-358-0440, Room 201B in Carthage
  • Assessor, personal property: 417-358-0437

Counter hours at the Collector's offices are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday. The Assessor's office follows state holidays and keeps the same weekday hours.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Jasper County?
sections.html:
Jasper County lies in the southwest corner of Missouri along the Kansas line. Carthage is the county seat, and Joplin, the largest city, is partly in Newton County. The county was organized in 1841 and has 638.51 square miles of land. Webb City, Carl Junction, Oronogo, Sarcoxie and Purcell are among its other cities, and its neighbors are Barton, Dade, Lawrence and Newton counties in Missouri plus Cherokee and Crawford counties in Kansas.

Interstate 44, Interstate 49 and the old Route 66 alignment cross the county, and the Joplin area is also a metropolitan statistical area. In May 2011 an EF5 tornado struck Joplin. For a seller, the practical point is that city, school and fire district levies differ across these towns, and one county bill carries all of them.

The Census Bureau's quick facts for the period 2020 to 2024 give a picture of the housing stock:

  • Estimated population on July 1, 2025: 127,428
  • Housing units: 56,504
  • Owner-occupied share: 62.8%
  • Median owner-occupied home value: $166,900
  • Median household income: $60,694

Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,219, and without one $491. Median gross rent is $973.

sections.h2: When are Jasper County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Statements are mailed in the first week of November, are due on receipt and turn delinquent after December 31. A mailed payment needs a USPS postmark on or before 12/31/26. The online payment page closes at 11:59 p.m. on 12/31/26, and money sent after that accrues interest and penalties once the site reopens in 2027. A payment postmarked late is returned unprocessed unless the late fees are included.

If no statement shows up by the end of November, the Collector asks you to call right away, and the office reminds owners that a missing statement does not remove the duty to pay. Technical trouble with a phone or online payment does not extend the statutory date, so plan for an in-person visit or the 24-hour drop box at either office if a website acts up.

sections.h2: How do I pay and what does it cost in Jasper County?
sections.html:
Ways to pay a Jasper County, MO tax statement, per the Collector's site
MethodDetail
In personCarthage or Joplin; cash, personal check, cashier's check, money order, credit or debit card
MailUSPS postmark of December 31 or earlier
OnlineCollector's website; closes 11:59 p.m. Dec. 31
E-check$2.00 fee
Credit card2.45% of the balance
Drop box24 hours at each office location
TelephoneToll-free number printed on the statement

The Collector explains that the service fee is not part of the tax and the county receives none of it. Under Missouri statute 139.055, only people who choose an electronic method pay that cost. Paying by check or in person avoids it.

sections.h2: How does the Jasper County Assessor decide what I owe on?
sections.html:
The Collector bills what the Assessor's records show, so errors in a mailing address, legal description or listed vehicle should go to the Assessor, not the Collector. For real estate, call 417-358-0440 and ask about your parcel's value and the notice you received.

Personal property works on a calendar of its own. Assessment lists are mailed in early January, due by March 1 without penalty, and may be filed online with the PIN from the mailed sheet. The Assessor does not accept emailed renditions. Tax is based on what you owned on January 1, even if you sold the vehicle later. Business owners assess equipment and furniture the same way, and landlords with rental or leasing space owe a tenant list by January 30.

A statement of non-assessment, which some call a tax waiver, can be used only to license a vehicle and requires bringing the title or registration to the office in person.

sections.h2: Can I appeal a Jasper County assessment?
sections.html:
Yes, through the county board of equalization. Missouri statute 138.060 directs that board to decide appeals from the assessor's valuation in a summary way, and it says there is no presumption that the assessor's number is right. The statute also puts the burden on the assessor in any other county when a value rose at least fifteen percent from the prior assessment without new construction or improvement.

Ask the Assessor's office, at 417-358-0440, for the filing deadline and hearing procedure for the current year, and bring comparable sales, a recent appraisal or a purchase contract. Pay by December 31 regardless of the appeal outcome, since interest and penalties start after that day.

sections.h2: What relief exists for older Jasper County homeowners?
sections.html:
The SB190 Senior Citizen Tax Credit is handled by the Collector. Applications for the most recent cycle ran from February 2 to May 31, 2026, at Room 107 in the Carthage courthouse, and could be filed online by QR code or PIN from a renewal notice. That window has closed, so ask the Collector when the next one opens.

  • The applicant must be 62 or older by midnight on December 31 of the initial credit year.
  • The home must be in Jasper County and be the applicant's primary residence.
  • The prior year's taxes must have been paid.

Renewal applications were accepted in the same period. The Missouri Department of Revenue runs its own Property Tax Credit for certain seniors and 100% disabled individuals, reachable at 573-751-3505, and that program is separate from the county credit.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about tax at closing in Jasper County?
sections.html:
Call the Collector for a current balance on the parcel before you set a closing date, since statements are due on receipt and become delinquent after December 31. Ask whether the escrow or title agent will pay the current year or prorate it, and put that in the contract. After the sale, the new owner should confirm the mailing address with the Assessor so that the November statement lands in the right mailbox.

Owners who inherited a house in Jasper County and are behind on earlier years should ask the Collector for the amount currently owed on each year before they quote a price to a buyer.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to pay Jasper County property tax?
faqs.a: December 31. Mail needs a USPS postmark on or before 12/31/26, and the online payment page shuts at 11:59 p.m. that night. After that date, interest and penalties apply.

faqs.q: Where do I pay in Jasper County if I live near Joplin?
faqs.a: You can pay at the Joplin Courts Building, 633 S. Pearl, at 417-625-4324, instead of driving to Carthage. Both offices have a 24-hour drop box.

faqs.q: How much extra does it cost to pay online in Jasper County?
faqs.a: An e-check carries a $2.00 fee and a credit card costs 2.45% of the balance. The county keeps none of it. A check or an in-person payment has no such charge.

faqs.q: I did not get my statement. Do I still owe?
faqs.a: Yes. The Collector says failing to receive a statement does not cancel the tax, and any penalty and interest still apply. Call if nothing arrives by the end of November.

faqs.q: Who do I call to fix my address or vehicle on the statement?
faqs.a: Call the Jasper County Assessor: 417-358-0440 for real estate or 417-358-0437 for personal property. The Collector bills only what the Assessor's records show.
